# Counterfeit and spurious medicine vendors in India, Jan 2025 to 7 October 2026: cases, parties, persons and FIRs

Compiled 7 October 2026 from police, regulator and press reports. Every row names the party (firm) and the person(s) reported with it. Names of accused persons are allegations from the cited reports unless a court has convicted.

## Bottom line

The full file holds 166 cases. 25 of them involve hospitals, clinics or government hospital supply chains directly. The four that matter most for a hospital pharmacy chain are below.

- **Bengaluru / Bidadi ICU-drug racket (Aug to Oct 2026).** Party: Krupa Healthcare, near Minerva Circle, Bengaluru, and an unlicensed repacking farmhouse at Hejjala/Dodderi near Bidadi toll gate. Persons: Veeresh Kumar Jain (owner of Krupa Healthcare, arrested 12 Sep 2026) and Prashanth Ranjan Babu, also reported as R. Prashanth (alleged kingpin, ex-medical representative, arrested at Kempegowda airport). Counterfeit ICU injections (Cefiavigent 2.5, Hizlam, Emblaveo with a Pfizer label) and cancer drugs were sold at discounts of up to 50 percent to more than 90 hospitals, clinics and shops through 15 or more medical representatives. Karnataka cancelled 16 distribution licences and suspended 8, including a Pfizer C&F depot. Suspect batch numbers are blocked on the Karnataka FDA portal and circulated to all states.
- **Delhi Crime Branch anti-cancer vial syndicate (FIR 12 Jul 2026, 17 arrested 20 Aug 2026).** Persons: Abhishek Vaishya, Shubham Kumar Chaudhary, Jaswant Sharma (oncology nursing in-charge of a hospital, who removed vials from the ward) and 14 others. Products: refilled or diverted Keytruda, Darzalex, Imfinzi, Erbitux, Opdyta, Gazyva, Bavencio and Adcetris vials, plus government supply diverted from PBM Hospital, Bikaner. No batch numbers were published.
- **Fake Alburel human albumin 20 percent, Maharashtra (three FIRs, Sep 2025 to Apr 2026).** Parties and persons: Shriram Healthcare, Pune (Shriram Nandkishor Chandak); R.S.L. Pharma, Pune (Rajesh Shantaram Jog); R.R.T. Pharma, Panvel; Maitri Pharmaceuticals and four distributors (Pune Vishrambaug FIR); Hitashi Pharmaceuticals and distributors (Nagpur Shantinagar FIR). Fake batches AM20025077 and AN20G25084 were seized. RituxiRel was also sampled.
- **Jackson Laboratories, Amritsar, TOCIN oxytocin batch I-7881 with nil oxytocin (May to Jun 2026).** Person: Managing Director Jugal Kishore. Five post-caesarean maternal deaths at Kota government hospitals; distributor Rajasthan Medical Hall, Kota, lost its licence; Punjab and Himachal manufacturing licences cancelled and a nationwide recall issued. Jackson batches also appeared in the Sep 2026 RML Hospital, Delhi, recall.

Also on the hospital radar: the Coldrif cough syrup diethylene glycol deaths (Sresan Pharmaceutical, Kancheepuram; owner G. Ranganathan; batch SR-13), the Lucknow cross-billing FIR against Health Plus (Ankur Awasthi), MK Pharma (Manish Bajpai), Ram Pharma (Govind Shukla) and Patient Care Surgical House, Saharanpur (Aijaz Ahmed), and the Puducherry fake Lupin and Sun Pharma brand racket run by N. Raja alias Valliappan, now with the CBI.

**Most urgent action:** pull every ICU injectable, oncology vial, human albumin, oxytocin and paediatric cough syrup bought since January 2025 from any party in Section 1 or Section 2, or from any non-authorised stockist at an unusual discount, into quarantine today, and verify batch numbers with the manufacturer before further use. Section 6 has the full checklist.

- **Parties / firms named:** Manglam Pharma, near bus stand, Paonta Sahib, Sirmaur (licensed wholesale drug distribution premises; licence valid up to December 25, 2028); unnamed Uttarakhand firm from which the APIs had been pilfered (probe underway there); two unnamed pharmaceutical manufacturing firms at Kala Amb and Parwanoo, Himachal Pradesh, which had purchased these APIs at below-market prices
- **Persons named:** Kewal Krishan (owner/proprietor of the raided wholesale firm; arrested under Section 17(B), Drugs and Co…, Manglam Pharma); competent person under the licence (unnamed) (taken into custody by inspecting officials along with the proprietor after failing to pro…, Manglam Pharma); two unnamed persons (arrested by regulators in Uttarakhand, where the spurious APIs were being sourced (both s…)
- **What happened:** CDSCO + HP Drugs Control Administration bust spurious-API supply racket at Manglam Pharma, Paonta Sahib; owner Kewal Krishan arrested under Sec 17(B) D&C Act. Agency: Joint team of Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) and Drugs Control Administration, Himachal Pradesh (Drugs Controller Dr Manish Kapoor); Uttarakhand regulators made two further arrests. Seizure value: not reported.
- **Products and brands:** Thiocolchicoside (API / raw material) (Thiocolchicoside) [genuine: not reported (API pilfered from an unnamed Uttarakhand firm)]; Azithromycin (API / raw material) (Azithromycin) [genuine: not reported (API pilfered from an unnamed Uttarakhand firm)]
- **FIR and legal details:** No FIR number or police station reported in either source. Firm owner Kewal Krishan arrested 'on Saturday' (Tribune, article dated 2025-07-08, i.e. after the 3 July raid) for trading in spurious drugs under Section 17(B) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940; the licence's competent person and the proprietor were 'taken into custody by inspecting officials' after failing to produce purchase bills. Drugs Controller directed the licensing authority and drug inspector concerned to expedite investigation and initiate legal action.
- **Hospital link:** none reported
- **Status:** Owner Kewal Krishan arrested (Sec 17(B) D&C Act); two more arrests by regulators in Uttarakhand; samples of both APIs sent for analysis; investigation ongoing as of 2025-07-08. No chargesheet, bail or licence-cancellation update could be obtained (search budget exhausted on 2026-10-07).
- **Verification notes:** Added from the Tribune: raid date July 3, 2025 and inspection continuing to the following evening; premises licensed for wholesale drug distribution with licence valid up to December 25, 2028; arrest of firm owner Kewal Krishan 'on Saturday' under Section 17(B) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 (article dated 2025-07-08, so the Saturday is after the July 3 raid); the competent person under the licence and the proprietor were taken into custody for failing to produce purchase bills; samples o…

#### M/s Welcure Remedies, Kala Amb (Sirmaur) loses manufacturing licences after export batch of Adenosine Injection (WADG25002A) declared spurious by CDTL Mumbai; fresh stop-production order 8 Sept 2026 (HP-2025-baddi-adenosine-licence, 2026-06)

- **Priority and evidence:** P3 regulatory alert; evidence level confirmed; confidence high.
- **Parties / firms named:** M/s Welcure Remedies, Kala Amb, Sirmaur district, Himachal Pradesh (manufacturer; all manufacturing licences under Form 25 and Form 28 cancelled); unnamed Mumbai-based marketing firm (marketed the injection; product approved only for domestic distribution but exported in violation of norms)
- **Persons named:** person not reported
- **What happened:** M/s Welcure Remedies, Kala Amb (Sirmaur) loses manufacturing licences after export batch of Adenosine Injection (WADG25002A) declared spurious by CDTL Mumbai; fresh stop-production order 8 Sept 2026. Agency: Himachal Pradesh State Drugs Control Administration (State Drugs Controller Dr Manish Kapoor; Assistant Licensing Authority, Kala Amb, Garima Sharma) acting on a DCGI communication based on the Government Analyst report of the Central Drugs Testing Laboratory (CDTL), Mumbai; joint risk-based inspec…. Seizure value: not reported.
- **Products and brands:** Adenosine Injection IP 6 mg/2 ml (brand given in Hindi by Punjab Kesari as 'काडिर्युरेक्स') (adenosine) [genuine: M/s Welcure Remedies, Kala Amb] batch WADG25002A
- **FIR and legal details:** No FIR or police station reported. Regulatory action only: sample declared 'spurious' under Section 17-B of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940; firm prohibited from manufacturing, selling or distributing any drugs under Section 18(c); all manufacturing licences issued under Form 25 and Form 28 cancelled and product permissions withdrawn (Punjab Kesari, 21 Jun 2026). Firm went in appeal and the stop-production orders were revoked. Second joint state-central inspection in August 2026 found lapses in microbiological testing and environmental monitoring (flagged in June) still unaddressed and the quality management system ineffective; Assistant Licensing Authority, Kala Amb issued fresh stop-production orders on 8 September 2026. Firm sought time to rectify; ordered not to commence production until satisfactory compliance and joint verification by regulators (Health Secretary Ashish Singhmar, 9 Sept 2026). Export angle under separate ongoing action. No arrests reported.
- **Verification notes:** New facts added: product described as Adenosine Injection IP 6 mg/2 ml with Hindi brand name 'काडिर्युरेक्स' (Punjab Kesari); sample declared spurious under Section 17-B of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940; all manufacturing licences under Form 25 and Form 28 cancelled with product permissions withdrawn (Punjab Kesari, 21 Jun 2026); Assistant Licensing Authority Garima Sharma confirmed the June action; State Drugs Controller Dr Manish Kapoor quoted; DCGI directed CDSCO Baddi to inspect jointly…

- **Parties / firms named:** 'SK Health Care' (also spelt 'SK Healthcare') Facebook page - sold branded medicines at 40-50% below MRP; M/s Nectar Herbs and Drugs, SIDCUL Sigaddi, Kotdwar, Pauri Garhwal - defunct unit, licence cancelled 2024, sealed 23 May 2026; earlier accused of fake Remdesivir (2021) and raided by Telangana Police (2024); Gaurav Tyagi's drug factory, Roorkee, Haridwar - earlier busted for fake medicines, closed ~2 years; Unlicensed manufacturing site at Bhagwanpur, Haridwar
- **Persons named:** Jatin Saini (arrested gang member; network run from Sambhal district, UP, 'SK Health Care' Facebook page); Gaurav Tyagi (arrested; owner of a Roorkee drug factory earlier caught making fake medicines (closed ~2…, Roorkee factory (own) / M/s Nectar Herbs and Drugs, Kotdwar); Mayank alias Monty (Gaurav Tyagi's cousin; co-manufacturer at Bhagwanpur, Haridwar (not reported arrested))
- **What happened:** Uttarakhand STF 'Operation Fake Pill': online counterfeit-medicine gang selling via 'SK Health Care' Facebook page busted; Jatin Saini and Gaurav Tyagi arrested; defunct Kotdwar unit M/s Nectar Herbs and Drugs sealed. Agency: Uttarakhand STF (SSP Ajay Singh) with Drug Department and local administration; case at Cyber Crime Police Station, STF Dehradun. Seizure value: not reported (recoveries: 22 boxes Gudcef Plus and 10 boxes Tydol 100 bought by STF as decoy customer; ~3 kg compressed tablets and 34 punch tools from Kotdwar unit).
- **Products and brands:** Gudcef Plus [genuine: Mankind]; Tydol 100 [genuine: Sun Pharma]; Copies of medicines of Sun Pharma, Zydus, Glenmark, Mankind, Macleods and other firms (incl. drugs for high blood pressure, fungal infection in women, prostate cancer; also NDPS-controlled medicines sold online) [genuine: Sun Pharma / Zydus / Glenmark / Mankind / Macleods]
- **FIR and legal details:** Case registered at Cyber Crime Police Station, STF Dehradun (ETV Bharat, 22-23 May 2026) under organised crime, cheating, forgery, creation of fake electronic records, IT Act and Copyright Act sections; Medical Dialogues (27 May 2026) reports BNS, IT Act and NDPS Act provisions. FIR number not reported. Gaurav Tyagi has 3 other fake-medicine cases in Haridwar, Dehradun and Maharashtra (ETV Bharat); Medical Dialogues says FIRs in Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Uttarakhand.
- **Hospital link:** none reported for this case. (Separate but related UP Drug Dept action, Agra, 21-23 May 2026: medicines made at an 'illegal factory in Roorkee' were sold in Agra; that raid also seized govt-hospital, ESI-hospital and military-hospital supply medicines worth ~Rs 1.5 crore from Agra wholesalers, but no hospital was named as a recipient of the SK Health Care gang's products.)
- **Status:** 2 arrested (Jatin Saini, Gaurav Tyagi); Kotdwar unit M/s Nectar Herbs and Drugs sealed on 23 May 2026 (licence already cancelled in 2024); forensic team sent; Roorkee and Kotdwar units being acted on by STF and Drug Department; search on for other members (incl. Mayank alias Monty); investigation of bank transactions, supply chain and medicine vendors ongoing. No chargesheet or bail reported.
- **Verification notes:** Products: STF decoy purchase via the SK Health Care page yielded 22 boxes of Gudcef Plus (Mankind) and 10 boxes of Tydol 100 (Sun Pharma), couriered from Gaya and Varanasi to Dehradun; gang copied Sun Pharma, Zydus, Glenmark, Mankind, Macleods brands with replica packaging, holograms and fake MRP; samples failed company lab tests; NDPS-controlled medicines also sold online; members used fake SIMs. Network run from Sambhal (UP) with links in Bihar, UP, Delhi, Chandigarh, Punjab, Uttarakhand (and…
- **Sources:** [medicaldialogues.in](https://medicaldialogues.in/news/industry/pharma/fake-cancer-bp-drugs-sold-via-facebook-at-50-discount-stf-busts-illegal-pharma-unit-in-roorkee-171503), [etvbharat.com](https://www.etvbharat.com/hi/state/uttarakhand-stf-arrested-two-members-of-gang-selling-fake-medicines-on-online-platforms-uts26052205331), [etvbharat.com](https://www.etvbharat.com/hi/state/stf-cracks-down-on-fake-drug-racket-seals-illegal-drug-factory-in-kotdwar-pauri-garhwal-uts26052303448), [etvbharat.com](https://www.etvbharat.com/en/state/uttarakhand-stf-seals-illegal-drug-manufacturing-facility-running-inter-state-operations-enn26052305485), [doonhorizon.in](https://doonhorizon.in/fake-medicine-wrappers-of-renowned-companies-and-poison-inside-fake-medicine-syndicate-caught-in-uttarakhand/), [etvbharat.com](https://www.etvbharat.com/hi/state/medicines-manufactured-in-an-illegal-factory-in-roorkee-uttarakhand-were-sold-in-agra-and-surrounding-districts-of-uttar-pradesh-ups26052502174), [etvbharat.com](https://www.etvbharat.com/hi/state/counterfeit-medicines-manufactured-at-an-illegal-factory-in-roorkee-uttarakhand-were-seized-in-agra-uts26052502822)

- **Parties / firms named:** Akshaya Pharma, Sadashiv Peth, Pune (retailer; samples collected 2025-10-16); Argus Medical Distributor, Sadashiv Peth, Pune (distributor); Ridhi Pharma, Karve Road, Erandwane, Pune (distributor); Sinna Pharma, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh (supplier); Mahival Medico, Gopalganj, Bihar (source; licence expired 2024-11-20)
- **Persons named:** Akshay Hasmukh Punia (medical shop owner (sample collection point), Akshaya Pharma); Amrit Bastimal Jain (distributor, Argus Medical Distributor); Manish Amrut Jain (distributor, Argus Medical Distributor); Rohit Popat Navadkar (distributor, Ridhi Pharma); Devendra Yadav (supplier, Sinna Pharma); Umang Abhay Rastogi (intermediary who received Rs 2,34,727 cash and passed it to Mahesh Garg); Mahesh Garg (supplier / recipient of payment); Soni Mahival (proprietor (licence expired 2024-11-20; shop no longer operational), Mahival Medico)

Agency: Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Pune (Joint Commissioner Girish Hukre; Drug Inspectors Shrikant Vishwasrao Patil and Vivek Khedkar); Pune Police, Vishrambaug Police Station (DCP Krushikesh Rawale). Seizure value: Rs 2.75 lakh (counterfeit medicines seized from Pune medical stores); Rs 2,34,727 paid in cash by Sinna Pharma to Umang Rastogi for the stock.
- **Products and brands:** Chymoral Forte (Trypsin Chymotrypsin tablets) [genuine: Torrent Pharmaceuticals (Sikkim unit)]
- **FIR and legal details:** Case lodged by Drug Inspector Shrikant Vishwasrao Patil (39) at Vishrambaug Police Station, Pune, against eight individuals (reported 2025-12-12). FIR number and sections not reported.
- **Hospital link:** none reported
- **Status:** 8 booked; report says distributors and medical shop owners from Pune and accused persons from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar 'have been detained'; joint FDA-police investigation announced. Per RMSC MD Pukhraj Sen, procured medicines are quarantined at district drug stores and each batch tested by RMSC-authorised labs before release to hospitals via the e-medicine software; failed batches are rejected. Medicaldialogues (citing NDTV) says 'multiple drug batches supplied under the Chief Minister's Free Medicine Scheme failed quality tests'. No page names any hospital or states that NSQ batches reached hospitals/patients; RMSC says no shortage will result as medicines are bought from other firms.
- **Status:** 7 firms debarred in FY2025-26 (5 for five years for supplying substandard/adulterated medicines; 2 for three years for violating service conditions / non-supply); 40 products banned from procurement (with 3-year, 2-year and 18-month product bans listed); fines in six cases; described as the highest number of debarments in a single financial year since RMSC's inception (26 companies banned in total from 2011-12 to 2024-25). No arrests, FIR or prosecution reported.

## 5. Contaminated cough syrup cases (diethylene glycol and related)

#### Coldrif cough syrup (Sresan Pharmaceutical, Kancheepuram TN) DEG contamination 48.6% w/v, batch SR-13; child deaths in Chhindwara MP; 7 arrests, TN licence cancelled, ED PMLA attachment, MP HC bail refused (TN-MP-2025-10-coldrif-sresan-deg, 2025-10-04)

- **Priority and evidence:** P1 hospital supply; evidence level confirmed; confidence high.

Ltd., Shekhpur, Gujarat - ReLife (separate manufacturer in same WHO alert)

## 6. What to do now in your hospital pharmacies

**Quarantine and batch-check (today)**

1. Print Section 1 and Section 2. Check every purchase invoice since 1 January 2025 against the party names and the person names (owners and medical representatives). Any match: move the stock to a sealed quarantine shelf and stop dispensing.
2. Pull and hold, regardless of vendor: all human albumin 20 percent (Alburel batches AM20025077 and AN20G25084 were fake), all oxytocin (TOCIN batch I-7881 and 1-8386 from Jackson Laboratories), Coldrif batch SR-13, Respifresh TR batch R01GL2523, ReLife batch LSL25160, any Cefiavigent, Hizlam or Emblaveo injection not bought from the authorised Pfizer or manufacturer stockist, and any oncology vial (Keytruda, Opdivo, Opdyta, Darzalex, Imfinzi, Erbitux, Gazyva, Bavencio, Adcetris, Herceptin, Avastin) bought outside the manufacturer-authorised channel.
3. Compare the batch numbers of everything on the shelves against the batch column in Sections 1 and 4 and against the CDSCO monthly alerts (cdsco.gov.in, Notifications, Alerts). Karnataka has blocked the suspect Bidadi batches on its FDA portal and circulated them to all states; ask your state drug controller for that list.

**Verify before releasing stock**

1. Call the manufacturer's customer-care or anti-counterfeit helpline with the batch number, manufacturing date and expiry date. Pfizer, Roche, MSD, Glenmark, Alkem, Torrent, Sun Pharma, GSK and Reliance Life Sciences all have brand verification channels; Section 4 lists the notices found.
2. Scan the QR or barcode on the pack. Under the Schedule H2 rule the top 300 brands must carry a unique code with manufacturer, batch, expiry and licence details. A code that does not scan, scans to a different product, or repeats across packs is a red flag (Patna IGIMS case: two un-scannable branded medicines were held).
3. Check the supplier's drug licence number on every invoice against the state drug controller's licence register, and the GST number on the GST portal. The Lucknow and Delhi rackets ran on fake GST firms and cross-billing. A licence that is cancelled or suspended (Karnataka: 16 cancelled, 8 suspended) means the stock cannot be legitimately traced.
4. Physical checks for injectables and vials: crimp seal and flip-off cap integrity, printing quality and font, label alignment, expiry format, vial fill level and clarity, carton glue and perforations. Refilled vials were the method in the Delhi oncology syndicate; relabelled expired stock in new containers was the method at Bidadi.

**If you find suspect stock**

1. Do not return it to the vendor and do not accept a replacement or credit note. Seal it, label it "suspect, do not dispense", and keep it in the pharmacy under lock.
2. Inform the state drug inspector in writing the same day and ask them to draw samples under Section 23 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act. Report on the CDSCO portal (cdsco.gov.in, Report, spurious or adverse drug reports) and on the state Drugs Control Administration helpline.
3. Keep the purchase order, invoice, delivery challan, payment proof, the vendor's licence copy and the names of the medical representatives who sold it. Investigators in the Karnataka case served notices on more than 25 hospitals and asked exactly for this.
4. Tell the treating doctors which patients received which batch, and watch for therapeutic failure (infection not responding, albumin not raising levels, oxytocin not producing contraction) and unusual reactions. Record these as adverse drug reactions with the hospital pharmacovigilance committee.

**Purchase-side rules going forward**

1. Buy only from the manufacturer's authorised C&F agent or stockist. Ask each vendor for the manufacturer's authorisation letter and the chain of custody for high-value injectables.
2. Treat any offer of 30 to 60 percent below the stockist price for cancer drugs, ICU antibiotics, albumin, IVIG, insulin or vaccines as a counterfeit signal. Every racket in this file sold at a deep discount.
3. Insist on batch-wise invoices with manufacturer name, batch, manufacturing and expiry dates, and reconcile them with the manufacturer's own supply record when the value is high.
4. Rotate a monthly check of your vendor list against the CDSCO alerts, your state drug controller's cancellation orders, and the state medical services corporation blacklist (Karnataka KSMSCL, Telangana TGMSIDC, Uttar Pradesh UPMSCL, Madhya Pradesh MPPHSCL and Kerala KMSCL all blacklisted suppliers in this period).
5. Keep physician samples out of saleable stock and keep government-supply packs ("Not for sale") out entirely; both were resold by rackets in Agra, Delhi and Patna.

## 7. Coverage and caveats

- **Cases:** 166 after merging duplicates. Priority split: 25 hospital-supply, 35 major rackets, 66 regulatory alerts and licence actions, 40 other.
- **Evidence levels:** confirmed 83 (core facts seen on two or more opened pages), partially-confirmed 49 (one opened page, or some details unsupported), unverifiable 34 (no page could be opened; facts come from search-result summaries only). Treat unverifiable rows as leads to check, not findings.
- **Period:** January 2025 to 7 October 2026, with a few older cases kept because they shaped 2025-2026 enforcement (Ballari ringer lactate deaths, Nov 2024; Mira Road civic hospital, 2022).
- **CDSCO alerts:** the monthly alert PDFs were read directly only for January and February 2025 (10 spurious entries, 131 hospital-relevant NSQ entries). The remaining months to August 2026 are covered through press summaries of each alert (see the CDSCO case ids in Section 3). Batch-level NSQ lists for those months should be pulled from cdsco.gov.in before any stock audit.
- **What was cut short:** a direct read of state drug-control websites, the Karnataka Drugs Control public notices and a second deep-dive on the Bidadi case were interrupted by an account usage limit on 7 October 2026. The Bidadi case therefore rests on press reports and is marked partially-confirmed.
- **Search limits:** early search rounds ran under a per-turn web-search budget and a network block on news and government sites; the block was lifted later and every case was then re-checked by opening its sources.
- **Legal status:** this is news- and regulator-reported information, not legal advice. Named persons are accused, not convicted, unless the row says so.
